text: {"summary":"Task v5-resolver-long-hard-1, resolver family, stage 3 of 8 (28 actions remain). Future task contract: repair a two-file Python 3.11 project; entrypoint engine.solve(data); return complete replacement contents for allowlisted engine.py and rules.py, with values/order empty. No third-party libraries, tools, network, or workspace access. A stage pass is provisional.\nRequirements revealed so far: packages maps names to rows {version:int,deps:list}; roots maps names to inclusive [min,max]. Return {versions:{name:version}} for exactly the dependency closure of roots. Every active dependency {name,min,max} of each selected version must be installed within its inclusive range; choosing versions may require backtracking. Among feasible installations maximize the version vector in sorted order of ALL package names, using -1 for absent names. If impossible, return {error:unsatisfiable}. Versions need not be consecutive.\nCheckpoint artifact: engine.py imports resolve from rules and returns resolve(data). rules.py filters root rows by bounds, recursively enumerates rows, treats dependencies as names (not {name,min,max} constraints), and selects by lexicographic score; returns unsatisfiable if no assignment. Thus the recorded artifact does not implement the newly stated dependency range constraints. Earlier candidate artifacts and notes are historical; do not treat notes as verified. Public feedback reports stage 1: 2 checks passed; stage 2: 4 checks passed; checkpoint feedback: 4 checks passed. Stage 3 has public test examples but no supplied stage-3 receipt. Tests illustrate backtracking/lexicographic choice and inclusive bounds. Stages 4–8 requirements remain unknown. Trial notes are unverified; use only supplied public data."}
